+package pir
+
+import "example.com/util"
+
+// GF(2^128) arithmetic with polynomial x^128 + x^7 + x^2 + x + 1.
+// An entry is viewed as a polynomial: word 0 holds coefficients of
+// x^0..x^63 and word 1 holds coefficients of x^64..x^127.
+
+func gfMulByX(a util.DBEntry) util.DBEntry {
+	lo := a[0]
+	hi := a[1]
+	overflow := hi >> 63
+	nlo := lo << 1
+	nhi := (hi << 1) | (lo >> 63)
+	// x^128 = x^7 + x^2 + x + 1 (0x87 in low coefficients).
+	if overflow != 0 {
+		nlo ^= 0x87
+	}
+	return util.DBEntry{nlo, nhi}
+}
+
+// gfMulPowX multiplies a by x^b in GF(2^128).
+func gfMulPowX(a util.DBEntry, b uint64) util.DBEntry {
+	if b == 0 {
+		return a
+	}
+	lo := a[0]
+	hi := a[1]
+	overflow := hi >> (64 - b)
+	nlo := lo << b
+	nhi := (hi << b) | (lo >> (64 - b))
+	if overflow != 0 {
+		// overflow holds coefficients of x^128..x^(128+b-1);
+		// reduce x^(128+k) = x^k * (x^7+x^2+x+1).
+		var contrib uint64
+		// carryless multiply overflow by 0x87.
+		for i := uint(0); i < 8; i++ {
+			if (0x87>>i)&1 == 1 {
+				contrib ^= overflow << i
+			}
+		}
+		nlo ^= contrib
+	}
+	return util.DBEntry{nlo, nhi}
+}
+
+// gfPowElem returns the field element x^b.
+func gfPowElem(b uint64) util.DBEntry {
+	if b < 64 {
+		return util.DBEntry{uint64(1) << b, 0}
+	}
+	return util.DBEntry{0, uint64(1) << (b - 64)}
+}
+
+func gfTable(a util.DBEntry) [16]util.DBEntry {
+	// Nibble table for a: tab[i] = a * (polynomial of nibble i).
+	var tab [16]util.DBEntry
+	tab[1] = a
+	tab[2] = gfMulByX(a)
+	tab[3] = util.DBEntry{tab[2][0] ^ a[0], tab[2][1] ^ a[1]}
+	for i := 4; i < 16; i += 2 {
+		t := gfMulByX(tab[i>>1])
+		tab[i] = t
+		tab[i+1] = util.DBEntry{t[0] ^ a[0], t[1] ^ a[1]}
+	}
+	return tab
+}
+
+func gfMulWithTable(tab *[16]util.DBEntry, b util.DBEntry) util.DBEntry {
+	// Horner over nibbles of b, most significant first.
+	var res util.DBEntry
+	started := false
+	for n := 31; n >= 0; n-- {
+		var nib uint64
+		if n >= 16 {
+			nib = (b[1] >> uint((n-16)*4)) & 15
+		} else {
+			nib = (b[0] >> uint(n*4)) & 15
+		}
+		if !started {
+			if nib == 0 {
+				continue
+			}
+			res = tab[nib]
+			started = true
+			continue
+		}
+		res = gfMulPowX(res, 4)
+		if nib != 0 {
+			res[0] ^= tab[nib][0]
+			res[1] ^= tab[nib][1]
+		}
+	}
+	return res
+}
+
+func gfMul(a, b util.DBEntry) util.DBEntry {
+	tab := gfTable(a)
+	return gfMulWithTable(&tab, b)
+}
+
+func gfInv(a util.DBEntry) util.DBEntry {
+	// a^(2^128-2), exponent bits are 1 for positions 1..127.
+	res := util.DBEntry{1, 0}
+	// binary exponentiation scanning exponent from high to low.
+	// exponent = 2^128-2: bits 127..1 are 1, bit 0 is 0.
+	for i := 127; i >= 0; i-- {
+		res = gfMul(res, res)
+		if i >= 1 {
+			res = gfMul(res, a)
+		}
+	}
+	return res
+}
+
+// gfSolveVWithTable solves, in GF(2^128):
+//
+//	e0 = u xor v
+//	e1 = aX*u xor aY*v     where aX = x^bx, aY = x^by, bx != by
+//
+// and returns v, given tab = nibble table for (aX xor aY)^-1.
+func gfSolveVWithTable(e0, e1 util.DBEntry, bx uint64, tab *[16]util.DBEntry) util.DBEntry {
+	num := gfMulPowX(e0, bx)
+	num[0] ^= e1[0]
+	num[1] ^= e1[1]
+	return gfMulWithTable(tab, num)
+}
+
+func gfDenominator(bx, by uint64) util.DBEntry {
+	ax := gfPowElem(bx)
+	ay := gfPowElem(by)
+	ax[0] ^= ay[0]
+	ax[1] ^= ay[1]
+	return ax
+}

+// smallDBMode selects the offsets-only protocol used when the whole

+// database itself within the reference storage budget, so the server
+// only needs the explicit offsets and answers with a single parity
+// over the entries they address.
+func smallDBMode(p refwire.Params) bool {
+	return p.DBSize*16 <= 1<<20
+}
+

 // bytes this implementation sends instead. It runs in its own process and

+	if smallDBMode(p) {
+		keyBytes := int(p.SBNum) * 16
+		if len(referenceRequest) <= keyBytes {
+			return referenceRequest
+		}
+		out := make([]byte, len(referenceRequest)-keyBytes)
+		copy(out, referenceRequest[keyBytes:])
